title: Ramayana Set for Record Global Rollout Across 50,000 Screens
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's $200 million epic starring Ranbir Kapoor will release in more international screens than any Indian film in history, with Sony Pictures handling overseas distribution.
body:
• Ramayana will release across 50,000 international screens, the largest global rollout ever planned for an Indian film, with Sony Pictures as the international distributor.
  • The two-part epic carries a combined budget of approximately $400 million, more than doubling the previous Indian cinema record held by RRR.
  • Music by Oscar winners Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, with an IMAX-first filming approach, positions the film as a global cinematic event.
  • Part 1 arrives Diwali (November 6) 2026, with Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has secured what its makers call the largest international release ever planned for an Indian film: a rollout across 50,000 screens in overseas markets. The announcement, made alongside the release of the film's English lip-synced trailer on August 6, confirms the producers' ambition to position the mythological epic as a global theatrical event rather than a niche diaspora offering.

A Scale Without Precedent in Indian Cinema

The 50,000-screen international footprint dwarfs previous Indian releases. Even S.S. Rajamouli's RRR, which grossed around $160 million worldwide and became a cultural phenomenon, operated on a fraction of this distribution scale. Sony Pictures, which is handling international distribution, has been building momentum since the film's teaser premiered in Los Angeles in April 2026.

Producer Namit Malhotra, who also serves as CEO of the eight-time Oscar-winning VFX studio DNEG, has been candid about the film's ambitions. "It's fair to say that we are shoulder to shoulder with anything out there," Malhotra told Collider in April. "Whether it's Lord of the Rings or Avatar, it's important to note that Ramayana actually precedes a lot of these global IPs and global epics."

"I can now predict that Ramayana (in two parts) will become the first Indian global theatrical blockbuster ever. See you at the movies!"

— John Fithian, founding partner, The Fithian Group LLC

The $400 Million Gamble

The two-part Ramayana duology carries a combined production budget of approximately $400 million, placing Part 1 at around $200 million. This is a record for Indian cinema — more than double the reported $70 million budget of RRR and twice the $100 million earmarked for Rajamouli's upcoming Varanasi.

The investment is visible on screen. The film was shot for IMAX from the outset, with DNEG handling the visual effects. IMAX's chief content officer Jonathan Fischer called Ramayana: Part 1 "the most anticipated global film this year" at a recent event promoting the company's expansion plans.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1zip1rNaNYs

Hans Zimmer, A.R. Rahman, and the Sound of an Epic

The film's score brings together two Academy Award-winning composers: Hans Zimmer (Dune, the Christopher Nolan films) and A.R. Rahman (Slumdog Millionaire). Malhotra described receiving the first score as a defining moment. "My text to him was, 'How do you make a grown man cry?'" he recalled. "The moment I heard the music, I was like, 'We've got it.'"

The collaboration is more than a prestige play. By pairing a composer synonymous with Hollywood blockbusters with one of India's most celebrated musicians, the producers are engineering a sonic identity designed to resonate across cultural boundaries.

A Star-Studded Mythological Cast

Ranbir Kapoor leads as Lord Rama, with Sai Pallavi as Sita, Kannada superstar Yash as the demon king Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The casting bridges Hindi cinema, South Indian film industries, and global appeal — a deliberate strategy to ensure the film transcends regional boundaries within India as well.

Based on the ancient Sanskrit text by the poet Valmiki, the film tells the story of an exiled prince who must rescue his wife from a demonic king — a narrative Malhotra argues served as the blueprint for stories like Avatar and The Lord of the Rings.

What This Means for Indian Cinema Globally

For the Indian diaspora and global audiences alike, Ramayana represents a test case. If it succeeds at the scale its producers envision, it could fundamentally alter how Indian films are financed, distributed, and marketed worldwide. The CinemaCon presentations, where top exhibition companies from the U.S., Canada, Latin America, Europe, and Australia attended private screenings, suggest the global exhibition industry is treating this as a serious commercial prospect rather than a cultural curiosity.

Part 1 is scheduled for release on November 6, 2026, coinciding with Diwali. Part 2 will follow during Diwali 2027.
nri_angle: The 50,000-screen global rollout means diaspora audiences will have unprecedented access to a major Indian film on par with Hollywood blockbusters in their local theaters.
author: Diaspora Desk
